889	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
890	// namespace but is not at one of its six exact locations:
891	//
892	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/ops
893	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
894	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/compact
895	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/query
896	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/list
897	//	GET  /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
898	//
899	// a missing "ops"/"state"/"compact"/"query"/"list"/"subscribe" segment, an extra
900	// segment, or a "crdt" segment in the keyword position (immediately past the
901	// document identifier) short of one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would
902	// answer those with a plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints
903	// must be a JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the
904	// guard itself.
905	//
906	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
907	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
908	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
909	// keeps its ordinary routes. Likewise "compact", "query" and "list" are
910	// endpoint keywords only in the fifth segment; a session or document literally
911	// named any of them is an ordinary identifier.
912	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
913		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
914		if !ok {
915			return false
916		}
917		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
918		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
919			return false
920		}
921		// Keyword position reached. The batch commit, the state read, the
922		// compaction, the batch lookup and the ordered listing are all exactly
923		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/{ops,state,compact,query,list};
924		// the subscription adds one trailing "subscribe" segment.
925		validOps := len(segs) == 5 &&
926			segs[0] != "" &&
927			segs[2] != "" &&
928			segs[4] == "ops"
929		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
930			segs[0] != "" &&
931			segs[2] != "" &&
932			segs[4] == "state"
933		validCompact := len(segs) == 5 &&
934			segs[0] != "" &&
935			segs[2] != "" &&
936			segs[4] == "compact"
937		validQuery := len(segs) == 5 &&
938			segs[0] != "" &&
939			segs[2] != "" &&
940			segs[4] == "query"
941		validList := len(segs) == 5 &&
942			segs[0] != "" &&
943			segs[2] != "" &&
944			segs[4] == "list"
945		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
946			segs[0] != "" &&
947			segs[2] != "" &&
948			segs[4] == "state" &&
949			segs[5] == "subscribe"
950		return !(validOps || validState || validCompact || validQuery || validList || validSubscribe)
951	}

963	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
964	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
965	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
966	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
967	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
968	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
969	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
970		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
971		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
972			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
973			return false
974		}
975	
976		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
977		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
978		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
979			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
980			return false
981		}
982		// Reject trailing data after the JSON value.
983		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
984			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
985			return false
986		}
987		return true
988	}

1402	// parseCursorPath reports whether raw is a decimal non-negative integer and
1403	// returns its value. Signs, fractions and other adornments are rejected.
1404	func parseCursorPath(raw string) (int64, bool) {
1405		if raw == "" {
1406			return 0, false
1407		}
1408		for _, c := range raw {
1409			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1410				return 0, false
1411			}
1412		}
1413		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1414		if err != nil {
1415			return 0, false
1416		}
1417		return n, true
1418	}

1420	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1421	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1422		var n int64
1423		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
1424			return 0, false
1425		}
1426		// Guard against values like 1.0 that Unmarshal into int64 on some inputs;
1427		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
1428		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
1429		if trimmed == "" || trimmed[0] == '-' {
1430			return 0, false
1431		}
1432		for _, c := range trimmed {
1433			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1434				return 0, false
1435			}
1436		}
1437		return n, true
1438	}
1439	
1440	// parsePositiveInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 1. Zero, floats,
1441	// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1442	func parsePositiveInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1443		n, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(raw)
1444		if !ok || n < 1 {
1445			return 0, false
1446		}
1447		return n, true
1448	}
1449	
1450	// isJSONObject reports whether raw decodes to a JSON object (not null, an
1451	// array or a scalar).
1452	func isJSONObject(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
1453		var m map[string]json.RawMessage
1454		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil || m == nil {
1455			return false
1456		}
1457		return true
1458	}

1542	// handleSessionPostChanges is the session-scoped batch commit over the same
1543	// change collection the session reads page:
1544	//
1545	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes
1546	//
1547	// The request body carries only the changes array — the calling device is the
1548	// session's owning device, resolved with the same identity rule as the
1549	// session reads, exports and subscriptions; no new credential is introduced
1550	// and no device id travels in the body. Per-element semantics and the success
1551	// body are byte-identical to the document-level commit: results arrive in
1552	// request order, each naming its id, whether it was created and the cursor it
1553	// was assigned. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400),
1554	// session existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict
1555	// is taken inside the commit transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing —
1556	// and a payload/device mismatch against an existing id is a 409 reporting the
1557	// conflicting id. Every rejection leaves the log untouched.
1558	func handleSessionPostChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1559		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1560		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1561

1563		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1564			return
1565		}
1566		if len(req.Changes) == 0 {
1567			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
1568			return
1569		}
1570	
1571		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Changes))
1572		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Changes))
1573		for i, c := range req.Changes {
1574			if c.ID == "" {
1575				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
1576				return
1577			}
1578			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
1579				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
1580				return
1581			}
1582			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
1583				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
1584				return
1585			}
1586			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}
1587			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: c.ID, Payload: c.Payload}
1588		}

1590		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
1591		// malformed batch against an unknown session is still a 400.
1592		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1593		if err != nil {
1594			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1595				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/push"
30		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
31	)
32	
33	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
34	// shared database connection.
35	type App struct {
36		*store.Store
37	
38		events *events.Service
39		crdt   *crdt.Service
40	
41		// pushSubs is the process-wide, in-memory registry of the live push
42		// connections across both channels. It backs the device-scoped
43		// subscription management endpoints and holds no durable state.
44		pushSubs *push.Registry
45	
46		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
47		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
48		// it through their gates rather than this field.
49		Authz *authz.Service
50	}
51	
52	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
53	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
54	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
55	// leaves nothing behind.
56	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
57		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61	
62		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
63		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
64		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
65		if err != nil {
66			_ = kernel.Close()
67			return nil, err
68		}
69		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
70		if err != nil {
71			_ = kernel.Close()
72			return nil, err
73		}
74		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
75		if err != nil {
76			_ = kernel.Close()
77			return nil, err
78		}
79	
80		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
81		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
82		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
83		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
84		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
85	
86		return &App{
87			Store:    kernel,
88			events:   eventService,
89			crdt:     crdtService,
90			Authz:    permissions,
91			pushSubs: push.NewRegistry(),
92		}, nil
93	}
94	
95	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
96	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
97	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
98	
99	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
100		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
101	}
102	
103	// Events returns the change event service.
104	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
105	
106	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
107	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
108	
109	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
110	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
111	
112	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
113	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
114	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
115	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
116	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
117		a.events.InterruptWaits()
118		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
119	}
120	
121	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
122	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
123		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
124	}
125	
126	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
127	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
128	func (a *App) Close() error {
129		a.events.InterruptWaits()
130		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
131		a.events.WaitDrained()
132		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
133		return a.Store.Close()
134	}
135	
136	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
137	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
138		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
139	}
140	
141	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
142	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
143		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
144	}
145	
146	// PostSessionChanges commits a batch whose device identity was resolved from
147	// a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
148	// gated commit: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
149	// serialized transaction as the write, so a revoked device commits nothing.
150	func (a *App) PostSessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
151		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
152	}
153	
154	// ReplaySessionChanges replays an offline batch whose device identity was
155	// resolved from a session by the HTTP layer; it is the session counterpart
156	// to ReplayChanges and commits through the same gated transaction the
157	// session-scoped batch commit uses, so the two paths cannot drift.
158	func (a *App) ReplaySessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
159		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
160	}
161	
162	// MergeChange delegates to the change event service.
163	func (a *App) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
164		return a.events.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, c)
165	}
166	
167	// MergeSessionChange merges a single change whose device identity was resolved
168	// from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
169	// gated merge: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
170	// serialized transaction as the merge judgment and append, so a revoked device
171	// writes nothing and a rejected request observes no change content.
172	func (a *App) MergeSessionChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
173		return a.events.MergeChangeAuthorized(documentID, baseCursor, c)
174	}
175	
176	// PutSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
177	func (a *App) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
178		return a.events.PutSnapshot(documentID, cursor, state)
179	}
180	
181	// GetSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
182	func (a *App) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
183		return a.events.GetSnapshot(documentID, cursor)
184	}
185	
186	// ExportSnapshots delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
187	// interval has no upper bound.
188	func (a *App) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ExportedSnapshot, error) {
189		return a.events.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
190	}
191	
192	// RestoreSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
193	func (a *App) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
194		return a.events.RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
195	}
196	
197	// RestoreSessionSnapshot restores a snapshot as an ordinary change whose
198	// device identity was resolved from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to
199	// the change event service's gated restore: the registration/permission
200	// verdict is taken inside the same serialized transaction as the snapshot
201	// lookup and the append, so a revoked device writes nothing and a rejected
202	// request observes no snapshot or change content.
203	func (a *App) RestoreSessionSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
204		return a.events.RestoreSnapshotAuthorized(documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
205	}
206	
207	// PutSnapshotVersion binds an existing snapshot cursor to a stable version
208	// name, delegating to the change event service's gated transaction: the
209	// registration/permission verdict is taken before the snapshot and version
210	// are observed, so a rejected request exposes neither.
211	func (a *App) PutSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name string, cursor int64) (events.VersionResult, error) {
212		return a.events.PutSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name, cursor)
213	}
214	
215	// ListSnapshotVersions delegates to the change event service.
216	func (a *App) ListSnapshotVersions(documentID, deviceID string) ([]events.SnapshotVersion, error) {
217		return a.events.ListSnapshotVersions(documentID, deviceID)
218	}
219	
220	// GetSnapshotVersionState delegates to the change event service, resolving a
221	// version name to its snapshot cursor and stored state.
222	func (a *App) GetSnapshotVersionState(documentID, deviceID, name string) (int64, json.RawMessage, error) {
223		return a.events.GetSnapshotVersionState(documentID, deviceID, name)
224	}
225	
226	// RebindSnapshotVersion moves a version name onto another existing snapshot,
227	// delegating to the change event service's gated transaction.
228	func (a *App) RebindSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name string, cursor int64) (events.VersionResult, error) {
229		return a.events.RebindSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name, cursor)
230	}
231	
232	// DeleteSnapshotVersion hard-deletes one version marker, delegating to the
233	// change event service's gated transaction; the snapshot itself is untouched.
234	func (a *App) DeleteSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name string) error {
235		return a.events.DeleteSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, name)
236	}
237	
238	// RestoreSnapshotVersion restores the snapshot a version name points at as an
239	// ordinary change, delegating to the change event service's gated restore.
240	func (a *App) RestoreSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, changeID, name string) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
241		return a.events.RestoreSnapshotVersion(documentID, deviceID, changeID, name)
242	}
243	
244	// ListChanges delegates to the change event service.
245	func (a *App) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, error) {
246		return a.events.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
247	}
248	
249	// ExportChanges delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
250	// interval has no upper bound.
251	func (a *App) ExportChanges(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ListedChange, error) {
252		return a.events.ExportChanges(documentID, from, to)
253	}
254	
255	// GetChangesByIDs delegates to the change event service's read-only batch
256	// lookup: per-id found/compacted/missing answers in request order, gated on
257	// the calling device's registration and document permission.
258	func (a *App) GetChangesByIDs(documentID, deviceID string, ids []string) ([]events.ChangeLookup, error) {
259		return a.events.GetChangesByIDs(documentID, deviceID, ids)
260	}
261	
262	// WaitForChanges delegates to the change event service.
263	func (a *App) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, bool, error) {
264		return a.events.WaitForChanges(ctx, documentID, after, limit, wait)
265	}
266	
267	// DocumentExists delegates to the change event service.
268	func (a *App) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
269		return a.events.DocumentExists(documentID)
270	}
271	
272	// CompactChanges delegates to the change event service.
273	func (a *App) CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
274		return a.events.CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID)
275	}
276	
277	// CompactSessionChanges compacts a document's change log for a caller whose
278	// device identity was resolved from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to
279	// the change event service's gated compaction: the registration/permission
280	// verdict is taken inside the same serialized transaction as the trim, so a
281	// revoked device removes nothing and a rejected request observes no change
282	// content. It is the session counterpart to CompactChanges; the boundary,
283	// retained summaries and persistence semantics are identical.
284	func (a *App) CompactSessionChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
285		return a.events.CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID)
286	}
287	
288	// AddSubscription delegates to the change event service.
289	func (a *App) AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (wakes <-chan struct{}, revoked <-chan struct{}, deleted <-chan struct{}, unregister func()) {
290		return a.events.AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID)
291	}
292	
293	// DeregisterDevice removes a registered device together with every record it
294	// owns — its sessions, the attachments it created (chunks, sealed state and
295	// unfinished uploads included), the access grants it held, and its
296	// document-permission rows — all in one serialized transaction that commits
297	// synchronously. An unknown or already deregistered device yields
298	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing, so a repeat deregistration
299	// misses exactly the way a never-registered id does and concurrent calls take
300	// effect at most once. Shared digest-addressed content is reclaimed only when
301	// the last completed attachment referencing it is gone; other devices'
302	// changes, snapshots and document content are untouched.
303	//
304	// After the commit the same id may register again as a brand-new device — no
305	// session, permission or attachment is inherited — and every live
306	// subscription the device held across both push channels is ended
307	// immediately, stickily.
308	func (a *App) DeregisterDevice(deviceID string) error {
309		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
310		if err != nil {
311			return err
312		}
313		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
314	
315		if err := store.DeleteDeviceTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
316			return err
317		}
318		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
319			return err
320		}
321		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
322			return err
323		}
324	
325		// End the device's live subscriptions only after the cascade is durable:
326		// a reconnect attempt after the close finds the backing session gone
327		// (404), so the connection cannot immediately re-establish itself.
328		a.events.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
329		a.crdt.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
330		return nil
331	}
332	
333	// ---- Document-level deletion. ----
334	
335	// DeleteDocument removes a registered device's whole document in one
336	// serialized, synchronously committed transaction. The calling device is
337	// declared by deviceId — no new authentication is introduced.
338	//
339	// The fixed verdict order is taken inside the transaction, before any cleanup:
340	//
341	//   - an unregistered device yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound (404) and writes
342	//     nothing;
343	//   - a device whose permission for the document was revoked yields
344	//     store.ErrPermissionDenied (403) and no cleanup runs;
345	//   - a document with no durable data anywhere — never created or already
346	//     deleted — yields events.ErrDocumentNotFound (404) and writes nothing.
347	//
348	// On success every row of the document is removed as one judgment: its online
349	// and trimmed change log, the retained idempotency summaries, its snapshots
350	// and named snapshot-version markers, its CRDT state and the per-document
351	// permission ledger. The same id is a brand-new document afterward — the
352	// cursor space restarts at 1 — and inherits no history or version names.
353	// Concurrent deletes commit at most once because the existence verdict and
354	// the deletions share one immediate transaction on the single connection.
355	//
356	// Only after the commit is durable are the document's live subscriptions
357	// ended (close code 4420 on both push channels) and dropped from the
358	// management registry; other documents' and devices' connections are
359	// untouched.
360	func (a *App) DeleteDocument(documentID, deviceID string) error {
361		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
362		if err != nil {
363			return err
364		}
365		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
366	
367		// Registration first, then permission, both before any document content
368		// is observed: a rejected delete reveals nothing and cleans nothing.
369		if err := a.Authz.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
370			return err
371		}
372	
373		eventsExist, err := a.events.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
374		if err != nil {
375			return err
376		}
377		crdtExist, err := a.crdt.DocumentDataExistsTx(tx, documentID)
378		if err != nil {
379			return err
380		}
381		// A ledger-only deviation row also counts as document data, so a document
382		// whose only durable trace is a grant/revoke still deletes cleanly and the
383		// re-created id inherits no authorization state.
384		ledgerExist, err := a.Authz.DocumentHasRowsTx(tx, documentID)
385		if err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		if !eventsExist && !crdtExist && !ledgerExist {
389			return events.ErrDocumentNotFound
390		}
391	
392		if err := a.events.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
393			return err
394		}
395		if err := a.crdt.DeleteDocumentDataTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
396			return err
397		}
398		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDocumentPermissionsTx(tx, documentID); err != nil {
399			return err
400		}
401	
402		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
403			return err
404		}
405	
406		// End the document's live subscriptions on both channels and drop them
407		// from the management registry only after the cleanup is durable: the
408		// close is one-shot per connection, so a client re-subscribing to the
409		// now-fresh id opens a new connection and never reopens the ended ones.
410		a.events.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
411		a.crdt.SignalDocumentDeleted(documentID)
412		a.CloseDocumentPush(documentID)
413		return nil
414	}
415	
416	// ---- Permission service boundary. ----
417

419	func (a *App) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (bool, error) {

421	}

425		return a.Authz.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
426	}
427	
428	// ListDocumentPermissions delegates to the permission service.
429	func (a *App) ListDocumentPermissions(documentID string, limit, offset int64) ([]authz.PermissionEntry, error) {
430		return a.Authz.ListDocumentPermissions(documentID, limit, offset)
431	}
432	
433	// ---- CRDT state service boundary. ----
434	
435	// SubmitCRDTOps delegates to the CRDT state service.
436	func (a *App) SubmitCRDTOps(documentID, declaredType string, ops []crdt.Op) ([]crdt.Result, error) {
437		return a.crdt.SubmitOps(documentID, declaredType, ops)

443	}

448	}
449	
450	// CompactSessionCRDT compacts a document's CRDT state for a caller whose
451	// device identity was resolved from a session by the HTTP layer, delegating
452	// to the CRDT state service's gated compaction: the registration/permission
453	// verdict is taken inside the same serialized transaction as the trim, so a
454	// revoked device trims nothing and a rejected request observes no state
455	// content. It is the session counterpart to CompactCRDT; the trimming,
456	// retained identities, snapshot body and persistence semantics are
457	// identical.
458	func (a *App) CompactSessionCRDT(documentID, deviceID string) (crdt.Snapshot, error) {
459		return a.crdt.Compact(documentID, deviceID)
460	}
461	
462	// GetCRDTSnapshot delegates to the CRDT state service.
463	func (a *App) GetCRDTSnapshot(documentID string) (crdt.Snapshot, error) {
464		return a.crdt.GetSnapshot(documentID)
465	}
466	
467	// GetCRDTOpsByIDs delegates to the CRDT state service's read-only batch
468	// lookup: per-id found/compacted/missing answers in request order, gated on
469	// the calling device's registration and document permission.
470	func (a *App) GetCRDTOpsByIDs(documentID, deviceID string, ids []string) ([]crdt.OpLookup, error) {
471		return a.crdt.GetOpsByIDs(documentID, deviceID, ids)
472	}
473	
474	// ListCRDTOps delegates to the CRDT state service's read-only ordered
475	// listing: one limit/offset page of the document's online operations in
476	// ascending id order plus the total number of operations compaction trimmed,
477	// gated on the calling device's registration and document permission.
478	func (a *App) ListCRDTOps(documentID, deviceID string, limit, offset int64) (crdt.OpList, error) {
479		return a.crdt.ListOps(documentID, deviceID, limit, offset)
480	}
481	
482	// OpenCRDTSubscription delegates to the CRDT state service.
483	func (a *App) OpenCRDTSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (*crdt.State, *crdt.Subscription, func(), error) {
484		return a.crdt.OpenSubscription(documentID, deviceID)
485	}
486	
487	// AddCRDTSubscription delegates to the CRDT state service.
488	func (a *App) AddCRDTSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (*crdt.Subscription, func()) {
489		return a.crdt.AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID)
490	}
491	
492	// RegisterPush records one freshly established push connection in the
493	// process-wide in-memory registry. The returned subscription carries the
494	// server-allocated id and the one-shot active-cancel signal; the connection
495	// layer removes it when the connection ends.
496	func (a *App) RegisterPush(deviceID, documentID string, kind push.Kind, cursor int64) *push.Subscription {
497		return a.pushSubs.Register(deviceID, documentID, kind, cursor)
498	}
499	
500	// UnregisterPush removes an ended push connection.
501	func (a *App) UnregisterPush(subscriptionID string) {
502		a.pushSubs.Unregister(subscriptionID)
503	}
504	
505	// ListPushSubscriptions returns the device's live push connections across
506	// both channels in establishment order. It is a pure memory view.
507	func (a *App) ListPushSubscriptions(deviceID string) []push.Info {
508		return a.pushSubs.List(deviceID)
509	}
510	
511	// CancelPushSubscription actively ends one of the device's live push
512	// connections. It returns false when the id is unknown, already gone, or owned
513	// by another device; those cases are one indistinguishable 404 at the edge.
514	func (a *App) CancelPushSubscription(deviceID, subscriptionID string) bool {
515		return a.pushSubs.Cancel(deviceID, subscriptionID)
516	}
517	
518	// CloseDocumentPush ends every live push connection subscribed to documentID,
519	// across both channels and every owning device, after its deletion committed.
520	// Other documents' connections are untouched.
521	func (a *App) CloseDocumentPush(documentID string) {
522		a.pushSubs.CloseDocument(documentID)
523	}

1	// Package store is the durable kernel shared by the internal services: it
2	// owns the SQLite database handle and the registration layer (devices and
3	// sessions) plus resumable attachments.
4	//
5	// The business services layered on top of the kernel — the change event log,
6	// the permission ledger and the CRDT state — live in their own packages and
7	// cooperate only through their internal interfaces. They all share this one
8	// handle: it opens a single pooled connection with immediate write
9	// transactions, so every service's transactional judgment is serialized on
10	// the same connection and no batch is ever half written.
11	//
12	// Devices and sessions form the registration layer. A device registers with a
13	// client-supplied id; a session belongs to exactly one registered device and
14	// is addressed by its own client-supplied id. Registration and session
15	// creation are idempotent re-posts: the first call creates, an identical
16	// repeat does not. A session id already owned by another device is a
17	// conflict, never silently re-homed. Deletes are owner-scoped and hard: a
18	// repeat delete, another device, and a cross-device path all miss with 404,
19	// after which the id is free to be created again. A device itself can
20	// deregister: the device row and everything it owns — its sessions and the
21	// attachments it created, chunks and grants included — vanish in one
22	// serialized transaction, a repeat or never-registered deregistration misses
23	// with 404 and writes nothing, and the freed id registers again as a
24	// brand-new device.
25	//
26	// Attachments are resumable chunked uploads owned by the registered device
27	// that created them. Creation pins the declared total size, chunk size and
28	// SHA-256 digest; chunks land in any order and are stored durably as they
29	// arrive, so an interrupted upload resumes after a restart with its
30	// idempotency and conflict decisions intact. Finishing concatenates the
31	// chunks, verifies the digest and seals the upload; a sealed upload is
32	// immutable and rejects every further chunk write. Finished content is
33	// addressed by digest, so a second attachment with the same digest and size
34	// reuses the stored bytes instead of copying them. The creator may grant
35	// other registered devices read-only access per attachment; every
36	// (attachment, device) pair starts unauthorized, grants and revokes commit in
37	// the same serialized way, and access never widens the write paths. Deletes
38	// are owner-scoped and hard: the record, its chunks and its grants vanish in
39	// one serialized transaction, a repeat delete misses with 404, the id is free
40	// to be created again, and the shared content bytes are reclaimed once the
41	// last completed attachment referencing them is gone.
42	package store
43	
44	import (
45		"database/sql"
46		"encoding/json"
47		"errors"
48		"fmt"
49	
50		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
51	)
52	
53	// ErrDeviceNotFound reports that an operation targets a device id that was
54	// never registered. Services map it to 404; nothing is written.
55	var ErrDeviceNotFound = errors.New("device not found")
56	
57	// ErrPermissionDenied reports that a device's access to a document has been
58	// revoked. Services map it to 403; nothing is written and no document content
59	// is exposed. It is a shared verdict produced by the permission service and
60	// consulted by every service that enforces the gate inside a transaction.
61	var ErrPermissionDenied = errors.New("device permission for this document has been revoked")
62	
63	// ErrSessionConflict reports that a session id already belongs to a different
64	// device. The session keeps its original owner; nothing is written. Services
65	// map it to 409.
66	type ErrSessionConflict struct {
67		ID string
68	}
69	
70	func (e *ErrSessionConflict) Error() string {
71		return fmt.Sprintf("session %q belongs to another device", e.ID)
72	}
73	
74	// ErrSessionNotFound reports that no live session matches the (device,
75	// session) pair: the session was never created, was already deleted, or
76	// belongs to another device. Services map it to 404.
77	var ErrSessionNotFound = errors.New("session not found")
78	
79	// DBTX is the subset of *sql.DB and *sql.Tx the services use for their
80	// serialized work, so judgments made "in the same transaction" (for example a
81	// permission gate followed by the gated write) run on one concrete connection
82	// whether the caller holds a transaction or the handle itself.
83	type DBTX interface {
84		Exec(query string, args ...any) (sql.Result, error)
85		Query(query string, args ...any) (*sql.Rows, error)
86		QueryRow(query string, args ...any) *sql.Row
87	}
88	
89	// Store is the durable kernel: one SQLite database handle together with the
90	// device, session and attachment data it owns.
91	type Store struct {
92		db *sql.DB
93	}
94	
95	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path. The empty path
96	// opens an in-memory database useful for tests.
97	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
98		if path == "" {
99			// With a single pooled connection this is a private, per-instance
100			// in-memory database (useful for tests).
101			path = "file::memory:"
102		}
103		// _txlock=immediate makes writers acquire the write lock at BEGIN, so
104		// concurrent batches serialize without SQLITE_BUSY deadlocks.
105		dsn := path + "?_txlock=immediate&_busy_timeout=5000&_journal_mode=WAL&_synchronous=FULL&_foreign_keys=on"
106		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil, err
109		}
110		// One connection avoids cross-connection locking surprises; writes are
111		// serialized by the immediate transaction anyway, and SQLite concurrency
112		// for readers does not help correctness here. It also keeps every
113		// service's transaction serialized on the same connection.
114		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
115		s := &Store{db: db}
116		if err := s.init(); err != nil {
117			_ = db.Close()
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		return s, nil
121	}
122	
123	// DB returns the underlying handle. The business services use it to open the
124	// serialized transactions their judgments run in; callers outside the
125	// internal packages never need it.
126	func (s *Store) DB() *sql.DB { return s.db }
127	
128	// Close releases the database handle.
129	func (s *Store) Close() error {
130		return s.db.Close()
131	}
132	
133	func (s *Store) init() error {
134		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
135	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices (
136		id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY
137	);
138	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
139		id        TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
140		device_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(id)
141	);
142	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS sessions_device_idx
143		ON sessions(device_id);
144	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachments (
145		id          TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
146		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(id),
147		total_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL,
148		chunk_size  INTEGER NOT NULL,
149		sha256      TEXT NOT NULL,
150		complete    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
151		reused      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
152		created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
153	);
154	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_chunks (
155		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
156		idx           INTEGER NOT NULL,
157		data          BLOB NOT NULL,
158		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, idx)
159	);
160	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_contents (
161		sha256 TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
162		size   INTEGER NOT NULL,
163		data   BLOB NOT NULL
164	);
165	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_access (
166		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
167		device_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
168		authorized    INTEGER NOT NULL,
169		granted_seq   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
170		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, device_id)
171	);
172	`)
173		if err != nil {
174			return err
175		}
176		if err := s.ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq(); err != nil {
177			return err
178		}
179		return s.ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq()
180	}
181	
182	// ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq adds the creation-order column to databases
183	// created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled in insertion
184	// (rowid) order so their relative listing order is unchanged; new rows take
185	// strictly larger values, so the sequence never reuses a value even after
186	// the newest attachment is deleted and its id created again.
187	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq() error {
188		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachments)`)
189		if err != nil {
190			return err
191		}
192		hasColumn := false
193		for rows.Next() {
194			var cid, notNull, pk int
195			var name, colType string
196			var dflt sql.NullString
197			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
198				_ = rows.Close()
199				return err
200			}
201			if name == "created_seq" {
202				hasColumn = true
203			}
204		}
205		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
206			_ = rows.Close()
207			return err
208		}
209		_ = rows.Close()
210		if hasColumn {
211			return nil
212		}
213		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
214			`ALTER TABLE attachments ADD COLUMN created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
215		); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		_, err = s.db.Exec(
219			`UPDATE attachments SET created_seq = (
220				SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attachments older WHERE older.rowid <= attachments.rowid
221			)`,
222		)
223		return err
224	}
225	
226	// ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq adds the grant-order column to access
227	// tables created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled one past the
228	// per-attachment maximum in insertion (rowid) order, so surviving grants keep
229	// a stable relative order; every new grant takes a strictly larger value, even
230	// after the previously newest grant was revoked, so a re-granted device lists
231	// at the position of its latest grant and a value is never reused.
232	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq() error {
233		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachment_access)`)
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		hasColumn := false
238		for rows.Next() {
239			var cid, notNull, pk int
240			var name, colType string
241			var dflt sql.NullString
242			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
243				_ = rows.Close()
244				return err
245			}
246			if name == "granted_seq" {
247				hasColumn = true
248			}
249		}
250		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
251			_ = rows.Close()
252			return err
253		}
254		_ = rows.Close()
255		if hasColumn {
256			return nil
257		}
258		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
259			`ALTER TABLE attachment_access ADD COLUMN granted_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
260		); err != nil {
261			return err
262		}
263		_, err = s.db.Exec(
264			`UPDATE attachment_access SET granted_seq = (
265				SELECT rn FROM (
266					SELECT rowid AS rid,
267					       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY attachment_id ORDER BY rowid) AS rn
268					FROM attachment_access
269				) WHERE rid = attachment_access.rowid
270			)`,
271		)
272		return err
273	}
274	
275	// RegisterDevice registers a device by client-supplied id. The first call for
276	// an id creates it and reports created=true; repeating the registration is
277	// idempotent (created=false). Device identity never changes.
278	func (s *Store) RegisterDevice(deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
279		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
280		if err != nil {
281			return false, err
282		}
283		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
284	
285		created, err = RegisterDeviceTx(tx, deviceID)
286		if err != nil {
287			return false, err
288		}
289		return created, tx.Commit()
290	}
291	
292	// RegisterDeviceTx is RegisterDevice against an existing transaction, so the
293	// services can resolve the registration layer as the first step of a larger
294	// serialized transaction (their permission/content gates then share it).
295	func RegisterDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
296		var exists bool
297		if err := q.QueryRow(
298			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
299		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
300			return false, err
301		}
302		if !exists {
303			if _, err := q.Exec(`INSERT INTO devices (id) VALUES (?)`, deviceID); err != nil {
304				return false, err
305			}
306			return true, nil
307		}
308		return false, nil
309	}
310	
311	// DeviceExistsTx reports whether deviceID is registered, evaluated inside q so
312	// a service's gate runs on the same transaction as the work it guards.
313	func DeviceExistsTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
314		var exists bool
315		if err := q.QueryRow(
316			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
317		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
318			return false, err
319		}
320		return exists, nil
321	}
322	
323	// CreateSession creates a session owned by deviceID with a client-supplied id.
324	//
325	//   - An unknown device yields ErrDeviceNotFound; nothing is written.
326	//   - A session id already owned by another device yields *ErrSessionConflict;
327	//     nothing is written and the owner is unchanged.
328	//   - Re-posting the same (device, session) pair is idempotent: created=false.
329	//
330	// A deleted session is gone for good, so its id can be registered again as a
331	// brand-new session (created=true). The lookup, owner check and insert run in
332	// one serialized transaction, so concurrent creates of the same session id
333	// cannot both create it.
334	func (s *Store) CreateSession(deviceID, sessionID string) (created bool, err error) {
335		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
336		if err != nil {
337			return false, err
338		}
339		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
340	
341		var deviceExists bool
342		if err := tx.QueryRow(
343			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
344		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
345			return false, err
346		}
347		if !deviceExists {
348			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
349		}
350	
351		var owner string
352		err = tx.QueryRow(
353			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
354		).Scan(&owner)
355		switch {
356		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
357			if _, err := tx.Exec(
358				`INSERT INTO sessions (id, device_id) VALUES (?, ?)`,
359				sessionID, deviceID,
360			); err != nil {
361				return false, err
362			}
363			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
364				return false, err
365			}
366			return true, nil
367		case err != nil:
368			return false, err
369		}
370	
371		if owner != deviceID {
372			return false, &ErrSessionConflict{ID: sessionID}
373		}
374		return false, tx.Commit()
375	}
376	
377	// DeleteSession removes the live session matching the (deviceID, sessionID)
378	// pair. Any miss — the session does not exist, was already deleted, or belongs
379	// to another device — returns ErrSessionNotFound and changes nothing. The
380	// check and the delete run in one transaction, so a concurrent create cannot
381	// interleave and a repeat delete still misses; the removal is committed to
382	// disk before the call returns.
383	func (s *Store) DeleteSession(deviceID, sessionID string) error {
384		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
385		if err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
389	
390		var owner string
391		err = tx.QueryRow(
392			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
393		).Scan(&owner)
394		switch {
395		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
396			return ErrSessionNotFound
397		case err != nil:
398			return err
399		}
400		if owner != deviceID {
401			return ErrSessionNotFound
402		}
403	
404		if _, err := tx.Exec(
405			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
406			sessionID, deviceID,
407		); err != nil {
408			return err
409		}
410		return tx.Commit()
411	}
412	
413	// ListSessions returns the page of live session ids owned by deviceID, each
414	// appearing at most once, sorted lexicographically by id ascending and paged
415	// by limit/offset as a slice over that fixed order — so with no intervening
416	// create or delete, successive pages neither repeat nor skip an id, and an
417	// offset past the end yields an empty (non-nil) slice and no error. An
418	// unregistered device yields ErrDeviceNotFound and no listing. The read runs
419	// in one serialized transaction and writes nothing; deleted sessions are
420	// absent, and a device deregistration removes every session it owned first.
421	func (s *Store) ListSessions(deviceID string, limit, offset int64) ([]string, error) {
422		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
423		if err != nil {
424			return nil, err
425		}
426		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
427	
428		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(tx, deviceID)
429		if err != nil {
430			return nil, err
431		}
432		if !exists {
433			return nil, ErrDeviceNotFound
434		}
435	
436		rows, err := tx.Query(
437			`SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE device_id = ?
438			 ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`,
439			deviceID, limit, offset,
440		)
441		if err != nil {
442			return nil, err
443		}
444		ids := make([]string, 0)
445		for rows.Next() {
446			var id string
447			if err := rows.Scan(&id); err != nil {
448				_ = rows.Close()
449				return nil, err
450			}
451			ids = append(ids, id)
452		}
453		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
454			_ = rows.Close()
455			return nil, err
456		}
457		_ = rows.Close()
458	
459		return ids, tx.Commit()
460	}
461	
462	// DeleteDeviceTx deregisters deviceID and removes every record it owns, all
463	// inside the caller's serialized transaction:
464	//
465	//   - the device's sessions are hard-deleted, so their session-scoped reads
466	//     and subscriptions miss from then on;
467	//   - every attachment it created is removed together with its chunks, its
468	//     sealed/unfinished state and the access rows other devices held on it;
469	//   - the read grants the device itself held on other devices' attachments
470	//     are withdrawn;
471	//   - the device row is removed last (every child row goes first).
472	//
473	// Digest-addressed content is shared across attachments and is reclaimed only
474	// when no completed attachment still references a digest — exactly the rule
475	// of a single attachment delete — so another device's attachment with the same
476	// digest keeps its bytes and one deregistration by itself never reclaims
477	// shared content. The document permission ledger lives in the authz package
478	// and clears its own rows against the same transaction through
479	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx.
480	//
481	// An unknown (never registered or already deregistered) device yields
482	// ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing. Because the whole judgment runs in one
483	// immediate transaction on the single shared connection, concurrent
484	// deregistrations of the same device commit at most once and any concurrent
485	// chunk upload or finish either committed entirely before it or is rejected
486	// entirely afterward — no half-written record survives.
487	func DeleteDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) error {
488		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
489		if err != nil {
490			return err
491		}
492		if !exists {
493			return ErrDeviceNotFound
494		}
495	
496		// Remember the digests of the device's completed attachments before their
497		// rows vanish: each is a candidate for content reclamation once every
498		// owned attachment is gone. DISTINCT because several of the device's
499		// attachments may share the same digest-addressed content.
500		rows, err := q.Query(
501			`SELECT DISTINCT sha256 FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ? AND complete = 1`,
502			deviceID,
503		)
504		if err != nil {
505			return err
506		}
507		var digests []string
508		for rows.Next() {
509			var digest string
510			if err := rows.Scan(&digest); err != nil {
511				_ = rows.Close()
512				return err
513			}
514			digests = append(digests, digest)
515		}
516		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
517			_ = rows.Close()
518			return err
519		}

521			return err

525		// attachments (rows naming it as the grantee), then remove the access
526		// rosters of the attachments it created before the attachment rows those
527		// rosters reference are deleted.

530		); err != nil {
531			return err
532		}
533		if _, err := q.Exec(

536			deviceID,
537		); err != nil {
538			return err
539		}
540		if _, err := q.Exec(
541			`DELETE FROM attachment_chunks
542			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
543			deviceID,
544		); err != nil {
545			return err
546		}
547		if _, err := q.Exec(

549		); err != nil {

553		// Reclaim each digest-addressed content only when no surviving completed
554		// attachment — owned by another device, or by the deregistered device in
555		// an impossible re-read — still references it.
556		for _, digest := range digests {
557			var stillReferenced bool
558			if err := q.QueryRow(
559				`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM attachments WHERE sha256 = ? AND complete = 1)`,
560				digest,
561			).Scan(&stillReferenced); err != nil {
562				return err
563			}
564			if !stillReferenced {

566					`DELETE FROM attachment_contents WHERE sha256 = ?`, digest,
567				); err != nil {
568					return err
569				}
570			}
571		}

573		if _, err := q.Exec(
574			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
575		); err != nil {
576			return err
577		}

579			`DELETE FROM devices WHERE id = ?`, deviceID,
580		); err != nil {
581			return err
582		}

584	}

587	// is the non-transactional counterpart to DeviceExistsTx, used by the

601		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {

603		}

605	}

611		var deviceID string
612		err := s.db.QueryRow(
613			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
614		).Scan(&deviceID)
615		switch {
616		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
617			return "", ErrSessionNotFound
618		case err != nil:
619			return "", err
620		default:
621			return deviceID, nil
622		}
623	}

625	// JSONEqual reports whether two payloads are equal after JSON decoding, so
626	// 1 and 1.0, or {"a":1,"b":2} and {"b":2,"a":1}, compare equal. It is shared
627	// verbatim by the change event and CRDT services' idempotency judgments.
628	func JSONEqual(a, b json.RawMessage) bool {
629		var va, vb any
630		if err := json.Unmarshal(a, &va); err != nil {
631			return false
632		}
633		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &vb); err != nil {
634			return false
635		}
636		return deepEqual(va, vb)
637	}
638	
639	func deepEqual(a, b any) bool {
640		switch av := a.(type) {
641		case nil:
642			return b == nil
643		case bool:
644			bv, ok := b.(bool)
645			return ok && av == bv
646		case string:
647			bv, ok := b.(string)
648			return ok && av == bv
649		case float64:
650			bv, ok := b.(float64)
651			return ok && av == bv
652		case []any:
653			bv, ok := b.([]any)
654			if !ok || len(av) != len(bv) {
655				return false
656			}
657			for i := range av {
658				if !deepEqual(av[i], bv[i]) {
659					return false
660				}
661			}
662			return true
663		case map[string]any:
664			bv, ok := b.(map[string]any)
665			if !ok || len(av) != len(bv) {
666				return false
667			}
668			for k, v := range av {
669				w, exists := bv[k]
670				if !exists || !deepEqual(v, w) {
671					return false
672				}
673			}
674			return true
675		default:
676			return false
677		}
678	}

1	// Package events is the change event service: the durable per-document change
2	// log together with everything written on top of it.
3	//
4	// Within a document every change has a client-supplied id. New ids receive a
5	// monotonically increasing cursor; re-posting an existing id is idempotent
6	// only when the deviceId and decoded JSON payload match, otherwise it is a
7	// conflict. Valid batches commit atomically in one serialized transaction, so
8	// cursors never repeat and no record is partially written, even under
9	// concurrent writers. Ordinary posts, offline replays, merges and snapshot
10	// restores all allocate from the same per-document contiguous cursor space.
11	//
12	// A document may also carry snapshots: caller-supplied JSON states pinned to
13	// existing change cursors. Snapshots are write-once per cursor — a matching
14	// re-post is idempotent, a differing one a conflict — and live apart from the
15	// change log. A restore appends an ordinary change whose payload is a
16	// snapshot's state, recording its provenance so a repeated restore after a
17	// restart keeps the same idempotency/conflict decisions.
18	//
19	// Reads page by cursor in ascending order. The session view and the document
20	// view are the same read; the HTTP layer adds the session/permission checks.
21	// Long polling and push subscriptions are in-memory observers of commits:
22	// they register before the confirming read, hold no durable state, and are
23	// woken only after a change-bearing transaction has committed.
24	//
25	// The service owns only its own tables. The registration and permission
26	// layers are reached through its Gate interface, so a replay or merge never
27	// reaches into another service's storage.
28	package events
29	
30	import (
31		"encoding/json"
32		"errors"
33		"fmt"
34	)
35	
36	// ErrStoreClosing reports that the service is shutting down and parked long
37	// polls have been woken so they can return without writing anything. The
38	// caller maps it to 503.
39	var ErrStoreClosing = errors.New("store is closing")
40	
41	// Change is one element of an inbound batch or one row of a listing.
42	type Change struct {
43		ID       string          // client-supplied change id, unique per document
44		DeviceID string          // originating device
45		Payload  json.RawMessage // decoded JSON value, stored verbatim
46	}
47	
48	// Result reports the outcome for one element of an accepted batch.
49	type Result struct {
50		ID      string `json:"id"`
51		Created bool   `json:"created"`
52		Cursor  int64  `json:"cursor"`
53	}
54	
55	// ListedChange is one row in a ListChanges response.
56	type ListedChange struct {
57		ID       string          `json:"id"`
58		DeviceID string          `json:"deviceId"`
59		Payload  json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
60		Cursor   int64           `json:"cursor"`
61	}
62	
63	// MergeResult reports the outcome of an accepted MergeChange. Outcome is one
64	// of "idempotent", "applied" or "merged".
65	type MergeResult struct {
66		ID      string  `json:"id"`
67		Outcome string  `json:"outcome"`
68		Cursor  int64   `json:"cursor"`
69		Result  *Result `json:"result,omitempty"`
70	}
71	
72	// ErrConflict reports that a batch references an existing change id with a
73	// different deviceId or payload. The whole batch is rejected.
74	type ErrConflict struct {
75		ID string
76	}
77	
78	func (e *ErrConflict) Error() string {
79		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting change %q for document", e.ID)
80	}
81	
82	// ErrStaleCursor reports that a merge targets a base cursor for an unknown
83	// document, or a base cursor greater than the document's current cursor. The
84	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
85	var ErrStaleCursor = errors.New("baseCursor is unknown or ahead of the current cursor")
86	
87	// ErrSnapshotBase reports that a snapshot targets an unknown document or a
88	// cursor that is not an existing change cursor of the document. The caller
89	// maps it to 400; nothing is written.
90	var ErrSnapshotBase = errors.New("snapshot cursor is not an existing cursor of the document")
91	
92	// ErrCompactedBase reports that a merge targets a base cursor below the
93	// document's compaction boundary: the changes it would be checked against
94	// have left the online log, so the conflict check cannot be completed. The
95	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
96	var ErrCompactedBase = errors.New("baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
97	
98	// ErrSnapshotNotFound reports that no snapshot exists for the document and
99	// cursor. The caller maps it to 404.
100	var ErrSnapshotNotFound = errors.New("snapshot not found")
101	
102	// ErrSnapshotConflict reports that a snapshot already exists for the document
103	// and cursor with a different state. The stored snapshot is left unchanged.
104	type ErrSnapshotConflict struct {
105		Cursor int64
106	}
107	
108	func (e *ErrSnapshotConflict) Error() string {
109		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting snapshot for cursor %d", e.Cursor)
110	}
111	
112	// ErrRestoreConflict reports that a restore references a change id that is
113	// already taken by an ordinary change, or by a prior restore whose deviceId,
114	// snapshot cursor or source state differs. Nothing is written; the caller maps
115	// it to 409.
116	type ErrRestoreConflict struct {
117		ID string
118	}
119	
120	func (e *ErrRestoreConflict) Error() string {
121		return fmt.Sprintf("change id %q conflicts with the change log", e.ID)
122	}
123	
124	// ExportedSnapshot is one row of an ExportSnapshots result.
125	type ExportedSnapshot struct {
126		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
127		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
128	}
129	
130	// ErrVersionConflict reports that a version registration or rename cannot be
131	// applied: the version name is already bound to a different snapshot cursor,
132	// or the requested bind would move an existing name (and zero writes is the
133	// required outcome). The caller maps it to 409.
134	type ErrVersionConflict struct {
135		Name string
136	}
137	
138	func (e *ErrVersionConflict) Error() string {
139		return fmt.Sprintf("snapshot version %q is bound to another cursor", e.Name)
140	}
141	
142	// ErrVersionNotFound reports that no snapshot version of the document carries
143	// the requested name. The caller maps it to 404.
144	var ErrVersionNotFound = errors.New("snapshot version not found")
145	
146	// SnapshotVersion is one row of a ListSnapshotVersions result: the version
147	// name together with the snapshot cursor it points at.
148	type SnapshotVersion struct {
149		Name   string `json:"name"`
150		Cursor int64  `json:"snapshotCursor"`
151	}
152	
153	// VersionResult reports the outcome of registering or renaming a snapshot
154	// version: the version name and the snapshot cursor it is bound to. An
155	// idempotent registration returns the same body as the first registration.
156	type VersionResult struct {
157		Name   string `json:"name"`
158		Cursor int64  `json:"snapshotCursor"`
159	}
160	
161	// RestoreResult reports the outcome of an accepted RestoreSnapshot.
162	type RestoreResult struct {
163		ID           string `json:"id"`
164		Created      bool   `json:"created"`
165		Cursor       int64  `json:"cursor"`
166		RestoredFrom int64  `json:"restoredFrom"`
167	}
168	
169	// schema is created when the service is constructed. Table and index shapes
170	// are unchanged from the pre-refactor layout, so data already on disk stays
171	// readable.
172	const schema = `
173	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS changes (
174		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
175		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
176		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
177		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
178		payload     BLOB NOT NULL,
179		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
180	);
181	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS changes_doc_cursor_idx
182		ON changes(document_id, cursor);
183	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshots (
184		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
185		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
186		state       BLOB NOT NULL,
187		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, cursor)
188	);
189	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS restores (
190		document_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
191		change_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
192		device_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
193		snapshot_cursor INTEGER NOT NULL,
194		change_cursor   INTEGER NOT NULL,
195		state           BLOB NOT NULL,
196		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, change_id)
197	);
198	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS restores_doc_cursor_idx
199		ON restores(document_id, change_cursor);
200	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_boundaries (
201		document_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
202		boundary    INTEGER NOT NULL
203	);
204	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_identities (
205		document_id   TEXT NOT NULL,

212	);
213	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshot_versions (

1	// Change-log compaction moves the old end of a document's change log out of
2	// the online tables without touching the cursor space the log shares with
3	// every write path.
4	//
5	// The compaction boundary is the greatest cursor that has a saved snapshot
6	// (zero when the document has none): everything at or below it is reproducible
7	// from a snapshot plus the surviving tail, so those rows leave the online log.
8	// A trimmed change is not forgotten, though — its id keeps a small canonical
9	// summary (the originating device, a digest of the payload and, for a restore,
10	// the snapshot it came from, plus the cursor it was first assigned) so the
11	// submission layer keeps answering idempotency and conflict exactly as before.
12	// The summary never participates in reads: pagination, long polling and
13	// subscriptions simply no longer see the trimmed rows, and the summary's
14	// fixed size means storage does not grow back to the pre-compaction shape.
15	//
16	// Compaction itself is not a change: it allocates no cursor, writes no change
17	// record and wakes no waiter or subscriber. The cursor space never resets —
18	// the next allocated cursor is one past the greater of the online maximum and
19	// the boundary — and the boundary, the summaries and the read results are
20	// durable across restarts.
21	
22	package events
23	
24	import (
25		"bytes"
26		"crypto/sha256"
27		"database/sql"
28		"encoding/json"
29		"errors"
30	
31		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
32	)
33	
34	// CompactChanges moves every change of documentID whose cursor is at or below
35	// the compaction boundary out of the online log, in one serialized
36	// transaction, and returns the boundary together with the number of changes
37	// removed by this call.
38	//
39	// The boundary is the greatest cursor with a saved snapshot, or zero when the
40	// document has no snapshot — compacting a snapshot-less or unknown document
41	// succeeds and removes nothing. The gate is enforced before any content is
42	// observed, exactly as in ReplayChanges: an unregistered device yields
43	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and a revoked device yields store.ErrPermissionDenied,
44	// and neither touches any state.
45	//
46	// Each trimmed id keeps its canonical summary (device, payload digest, restore
47	// provenance and first cursor) so re-posting it stays idempotent and a
48	// differing re-post stays a conflict. Compaction is idempotent: a repeat finds
49	// the same boundary, trims nothing and reports zero removed. It commits no
50	// change row, allocates no cursor and notifies no waiter or subscriber.
51	func (s *Service) CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
52		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
53		if err != nil {
54			return 0, 0, err
55		}
56		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
57	
58		// Registration and permission are enforced before any change content is
59		// observed, so a rejected compaction cannot reveal anything.
60		if s.gate != nil {
61			if err := s.gate.DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
62				return 0, 0, err
63			}
64		}
65	
66		// The boundary is the greatest cursor with a saved snapshot, 0 when the
67		// document has none (an unknown document included).
68		if err := tx.QueryRow(
69			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ?`,
70			documentID,
71		).Scan(&boundary); err != nil {
72			return 0, 0, err
73		}
74		stored, err := boundaryOfTx(tx, documentID)
75		if err != nil {
76			return 0, 0, err
77		}
78		if boundary <= stored {
79			// Nothing new to trim (a repeat compaction, or a snapshot-less
80			// document): report the standing boundary and remove nothing.
81			return stored, 0, tx.Commit()
82		}
83	
84		// Collect the rows leaving the online log before deleting them: each one
85		// first moves its canonical summary into the identity table.
86		type trimmed struct {
87			cursor  int64
88			id      string
89			device  string
90			payload []byte
91		}
92		rows, err := tx.Query(
93			`SELECT cursor, id, device_id, payload FROM changes
94			 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor <= ?
95			 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
96			documentID, boundary,
97		)
98		if err != nil {
99			return 0, 0, err
100		}
101		var dropping []trimmed
102		for rows.Next() {
103			var t trimmed
104			if err := rows.Scan(&t.cursor, &t.id, &t.device, &t.payload); err != nil {
105				_ = rows.Close()
106				return 0, 0, err
107			}
108			dropping = append(dropping, t)
109		}
110		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
111			_ = rows.Close()
112			return 0, 0, err
113		}
114		_ = rows.Close()
115	
116		for _, t := range dropping {
117			// A restored change also carries its provenance into the summary, so a
118			// repeated restore keeps its idempotency/conflict decision.
119			var restoredFrom sql.NullInt64
120			err := tx.QueryRow(
121				`SELECT snapshot_cursor FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_id = ?`,
122				documentID, t.id,
123			).Scan(&restoredFrom)
124			switch {
125			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
126				restoredFrom = sql.NullInt64{}
127			case err != nil:
128				return 0, 0, err
129			}
130			digest, err := payloadDigest(t.payload)
131			if err != nil {
132				return 0, 0, err
133			}
134			if _, err := tx.Exec(
135				`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO change_identities
136					(document_id, id, device_id, digest, cursor, restored_from)
137				 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
138				documentID, t.id, t.device, digest, t.cursor, restoredFrom,
139			); err != nil {
140				return 0, 0, err
141			}
142		}
143	
144		if _, err := tx.Exec(
145			`DELETE FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_cursor <= ?`,
146			documentID, boundary,
147		); err != nil {
148			return 0, 0, err
149		}
150		if _, err := tx.Exec(
151			`DELETE FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor <= ?`,
152			documentID, boundary,
153		); err != nil {
154			return 0, 0, err
155		}
156		if _, err := tx.Exec(
157			`INSERT INTO change_boundaries (document_id, boundary) VALUES (?, ?)
158			 ON CONFLICT (document_id) DO UPDATE SET boundary = excluded.boundary`,
159			documentID, boundary,
160		); err != nil {
161			return 0, 0, err
162		}
163	
164		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
165			return 0, 0, err
166		}
167		// Compaction is not a change: no waiter is woken and no subscriber is
168		// signaled, because no new change exists to observe.
169		return boundary, int64(len(dropping)), nil
170	}
171	
172	// boundaryOfTx returns the stored compaction boundary of documentID, or zero
173	// when the document was never compacted.
174	func boundaryOfTx(q store.DBTX, documentID string) (int64, error) {
175		var boundary int64
176		err := q.QueryRow(
177			`SELECT boundary FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?`,
178			documentID,
179		).Scan(&boundary)
180		switch {
181		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
182			return 0, nil
183		case err != nil:
184			return 0, err
185		default:
186			return boundary, nil
187		}
188	}
189	
190	// currentCursorTx returns the document's high-water mark: the greatest online
191	// cursor, or the compaction boundary when every change up to it has left the
192	// online log. The cursor space never resets, so a fully trimmed document
193	// continues from its boundary rather than from zero.
194	func currentCursorTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) (int64, error) {
195		var maxOnline int64
196		if err := tx.QueryRow(
197			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
198			documentID,
199		).Scan(&maxOnline); err != nil {
200			return 0, err
201		}
202		boundary, err := boundaryOfTx(tx, documentID)
203		if err != nil {
204			return 0, err
205		}
206		if boundary > maxOnline {
207			maxOnline = boundary
208		}
209		return maxOnline, nil
210	}
211	
212	// payloadDigest renders a payload in the canonical form JSONEqual compares —
213	// the decoded value re-encoded, so 1 and 1.0 or reordered object keys digest
214	// alike — and hashes it. The digest is the fixed-size stand-in for the payload
215	// in a trimmed change's retained summary.
216	func payloadDigest(payload json.RawMessage) ([]byte, error) {
217		var v any
218		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &v); err != nil {
219			return nil, err
220		}
221		canonical, err := json.Marshal(v)
222		if err != nil {
223			return nil, err
224		}
225		sum := sha256.Sum256(canonical)
226		return sum[:], nil
227	}
228	
229	// resolveTrimmedIdentity answers the submission question for an id whose
230	// online row is absent because compaction trimmed it. It returns found=true
231	// and the id's first cursor when the retained summary matches the incoming
232	// device and payload (an idempotent re-post), an *ErrConflict when a retained
233	// summary exists but differs, and found=false when no summary was retained (a
234	// genuinely new id).
235	func resolveTrimmedIdentity(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, c Change) (found bool, cursor int64, err error) {
236		var device string
237		var digest []byte
238		err = tx.QueryRow(
239			`SELECT device_id, digest, cursor FROM change_identities WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
240			documentID, c.ID,
241		).Scan(&device, &digest, &cursor)
242		switch {
243		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
244			return false, 0, nil
245		case err != nil:
246			return false, 0, err
247		}
248	
249		incoming, err := payloadDigest(c.Payload)
250		if err != nil {
251			return false, 0, err
252		}
253		if device != c.DeviceID || !bytes.Equal(digest, incoming) {
254			return false, 0, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
255		}
256		return true, cursor, nil
257	}

Key question: listing documents that the device's sessions have ever written changes to. 

I’ve confirmed the eligible sources of document IDs written by the device’s sessions. I initially considered using the change_identities table, but after verifying against the specification, I’ve ruled it out. The specification explicitly states that documents whose changes have been fully cleared no longer appear in the list, so the final eligible data source is only the online changes table.

I’ve further confirmed the rule logic is valid and testable, and verified that device identity information can be obtained through two valid channels, with the final query plan finalized.

I found there’s no field in the changes table to distinguish whether a write operation comes from a session or a direct document-level post by the same device, so the query can only be based on the device_id field. The expected implementation covers both session and direct document-level writes by the same device.

Given the test expectations and data model limitations, I’ve finalized the query using distinct document_id from the changes table filtered by device_id. The implementation covers both session and direct document-level writes by the device, and changes belonging to the deregistered device will survive the process, leading to a 404 when queried after deregistration.

I’ve verified that the query logic complies with relevant specifications, covering scenarios such as document deletion and compaction. Since the changes table is managed by the events service and separated from the store layer by package boundaries, I’ve finalized the design of a new list method in the events service, which will first check the device’s registration status via the store layer’s existing permission interface.

I’ve confirmed the events service’s dedicated list method is the cleanest implementation, with pagination aligned to spec, and finalized the API route. Next I’ll check the query parser used by the HTTP layer.

The ServeMux pattern works properly, with extra segments or wrong methods returning 400, and empty path segments being correctly filtered.

Per specification, path-related errors should return 400. The current DELETE logic for document paths incorrectly returns 400 for valid deregistration requests, so I will align the document collection's HTTP handling rules with the existing session rules for clarity.
